To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conductivity of glasses from 0.4 Li2O·0·6(xB2O1−x) Si2O4 increases from the silica (x=0) to the boron (x=1) region with an anomaly at 0.3.

The electrical conductivity increases with the substitution of SiO2 by B2O3, with an anomaly for x=0.30; the activation energy increases with the substitution, but the pre-exponential factor decreases; and the relaxation frequency increases with the substitution.

(1) electrical conductivity of glasses from Li2O–B2O3–SiO2 increases from the silica region to the boron region, (2) the activation energy of electrical conductivity is independent of the composition, and (3) the relaxation frequency increases from the silica-rich glasses to the boron-rich glasses, and then decreases in the boron-rich region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of glasses in the system 0.
the electrical properties of glasses with a high boron content, which have been less studied than glasses with a high silica content.
the electrical properties of glasses in the system Li2O–B2O3–SiO2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the substitution of SiO2 by B2O3 in this glass system does not change the activation energy, but increases both the conductivity and the pre-exponential factor.
the conductivity mechanism is mainly governed by the presence of the boron network former and the activation energy is mainly governed by its connectivity.
the electrical conductivity and the relaxation frequency are not directly related, but that both are related to the glass structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in this system, the electrical conductivity is not affected by the substitution of the glass former.
, in this system, the electrical properties are controlled by the presence of boron oxide.
the electrical properties of these glasses are dominated by the boron oxide network, and the lithium oxide network has a secondary influence on the electrical conductivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electrical conductivity and relaxation frequency are not directly correlated, as has been reported in the literature for other glass systems.
the relaxation frequency is a more reliable parameter than the activation energy for the study of glass-forming ability and fragility.
, in contrast to electrical conductivity, relaxation frequency is independent of the composition and is a function of the glass transition temperature only, as expected.
